lines.line: -What time is it now...
Ringing in my ears made me immediately jump out of bed. What? A siren?
I woke up, barely understanding what was happening. The sound stopped right after I woke up. The megaphones emitted one alarming note and fell silent. They don't even let you sleep...
-Oh, you're awake.
-Is this your doing?
How do you think I can control the siren? I have paws.
-Oh.
I looked out the window. Nothing is happening, not even a light in the windows. Very strange.
And that boy with a stick-gun... Maybe I just dreamed it all.
Maybe it's a test of the alert system?
But why at night? And what's the point of such tests if nothing ever happens in our city for years.
At least a fire or something, really.
-Huh?
-From where?
There was a stimulator on the windowsill, although the window was closed.
I flopped back onto the bed and didn't even notice when I started snoring again.
Crackling in my head. Pain. Alarm clock. For all the time I've lived, I never got used to waking up by alarm. Is today only Tuesday? You must be kidding!
I hope that Monday is a hard day, and everything that happened yesterday was an exception.
With a familiar hand gesture, I turn on the machine - Sonya sent a bunch of links.
Links to articles. Let's start with the first one...
Someone posted excerpts from someone's scientific work on the principles and effects of Fingerboxes...
There was an insane drawing with dimensions and materials. Is it worth buying a two-finger one, or should I save up for a three- or four-finger one?
I really want it, but I'm sorry to spend so much money on it.
-What's a Fingerbox?
-What?
Various Fingerbox options were discussed - plastic, steel, and wooden.
It's completely unclear what the purpose of the Fingerbox and Fingerboxing itself is, but one thing is clear -
Material matters. A plastic Fingerbox for a hundred bucks broke down in half a year.
The Q&A page was dedicated to Zhelemish.
As a child, I was fed Zhelemish. First my grandfather rubbed it on his back, then my dad on his heels.
And then, twenty years later, I grew up, moved to a big city to study. They invited me to a party and decided to prank me by mixing diphenhydramine into my beer. I drank the whole bottle - nothing.
Everyone is looking, amazed. And the poison doesn't affect me - Zhelemish inside me.
Once in an alley, a thug tried to stab me, but his hand slipped off the handle: it doesn't pierce my skin - tanned with Zhelemish.
I returned to my native village in the summer, and there was bad news: grandma passed away.
I came, and this Zhelemish is growing right over the graves, resembling human silhouettes, and nowhere else.
No one has ever found Zhelemish paste for sale.
A page discussing some strange kind of brick.
Visually - a pressed brown mass with an embossed stamp and the year of production.
Apparently, this brick was used in initiation rituals for the party, or something like that.
The legendary Middle Eastern Gavnyak.
According to the PROPER SOVIET STANDARD, it was mandatory to use at least 20% poppy straw by weight...
... and it was prohibited for chicken manure content to exceed 4.5% of the final product's weight.
Ah, they don't make it like that anymore.
The old-timers still remember with tears in their eyes THAT very taste of pre-war Gavnyak.
Several generations of Soviets grew up on the unforgettable taste, the bright aroma, and the MIND-BLOWING kick.
I really should quit this stuff.
What, it's nine o'clock already? The classes have already started!
I pulled the cord out of the socket, hastily brushed my teeth, put on my shoes, and dashed into the hallway.
Right, there's still a pack of cookies somewhere.
The usual path to school. Sometimes it feels like I live in some kind of tunnel. One end is in the classroom, the other is at home. Another in the park, one more in the club, and more, more, more...
And it feels like if you step off your designated path by one step - you'll just cease to exist. Damn, as if I physically can't turn anywhere else, or stay for a minute.
It feels like I just won't be able to interact with objects if they're not part of my usual environment. I feel like I'm starting to stop feeling alive...
And the scariest thing is - I have no desire or strength to resist it. Such nonsense.
Kir didn't come to walk me today. Maybe he got sick. The move must have weakened his body, and here we are.
Well, yesterday I had enough time to chat with him... I can reach school on my own, even in the dark - it seems I'm slowly getting used to it.
There's the holey school fence. They tried to close it during classes, but we're not the kind of people it can stop. So...
Everyone quickly understood everything, and now we're free again.
It looks like Alina is waiting for me at the fence. She's standing and shifting from foot to foot. Sweetheart. There she is - white shirt, old-fashioned blue skirt.
Pioneri used to wear these. Or maybe not.
-Mira!
Alina smiled slightly when she noticed me and waved.
-What are you doing here? The class has already started. You never come late.
-I just wanted to wait for you.
Alina glanced off to the side.
-I thought... maybe you'd like to skip school with me!
She seems nervous.
-Skip? Doesn't sound like you. You keep surprising me.
-Yes, I... I understand. My father keeps track of time and doesn't let me go out after school... So, I have no choice.
-You're already missing a lot; it's not worth risking it.
Alina thought about it and grew sad.
-Maybe you're right... But I want to spend time with you!
-I understand, but right now it's better for us to stay in school.
-Alright... Promise we'll go out together?
-Okay, I promise. We'll go out this week. Deal?
I walked through the gate toward the porch, and Alina reluctantly followed behind.
The door opened, and rows of classmates in gym uniforms ran toward us.
-Damn, is it gym class today? And I forgot my change clothes again...
-I'd lend you mine, but I'm suspended from classes...
-Yeah, I get it...
-Kalinina, why aren't you in uniform?!
-This is my uniform, what's wrong?
-The color doesn't follow the dress code! White top, black bottom!
-I don't have that...
-Fine, just get in line already.
Alina giggled into her hand and headed to the bench to watch the class do gym. She's probably bored... It would really be better if she just went for a walk instead.
On the field behind the school, an unfamiliar girl was already warming up. Maybe she's from another class?
Her height is huge; she's a couple of heads taller than me!
Stretching, she noticed the crowd and waved.
-So, this is your new girl - Kira. Don't mess with her, got it? Otherwise, you're all jerks...
Kira smiled.
-Hi everyone! Glad to see you all!
She has a heavy lisp. She's definitely going to be picked on...
-Alright, warm-up time. Don't just stand there! Then we'll play dodgeball!
-Pair up, and let's start.
Kira spotted me in the crowd and decided to come over and introduce herself.
Why she chose me as the first person to meet is unclear. Something about me attracts weirdos like Sonya, but what exactly, I have no idea.
She smiled and held out her hand.
-Ki-ra.
It took me a moment to figure out what to do in response.
-Oh, sorry, it's a habit...
Kira withdrew her hand and hid it behind her back.
-I'm Mira. So, you're going to study with us now?
-Yup! I came here from a big city, far, far away.
-Hmm... I feel like I've heard that before...
-What do you mean?
-A new kid came yesterday too - also from far away, and his name was Kir.
Kira laughed.
-Of course, he's my bro-ther. He didn't say he has a sis-ter?
-And... we're done! Everyone take your places, hurry up!

A few people set up the net between poles on the makeshift field. Kira stood in the middle of our side, and I positioned myself off to the side so as not to interfere with the others. I'm not much of a player... Kira struck a strange, almost sexy pose, stretching with her eyes closed as if showing her superiority over the others.
Someone served the ball, and the game began. None of the girls, except for her, moved from their spot, lazily hitting the ball, which often landed on our side, making the team lose points.
Kira darted across the court like a bullet, sending the ball back to the other side, shouting with each hit and breathing heavily.
Her feet dug powerfully into the ground, kicking up dust. Despite the seeming fragility of those long smooth legs, it was hard not to notice the large muscles.
Kira runs, suddenly stopping in place, skidding on the sand with her sneakers, slamming the incoming ball.
-Mira!
Again, the ball, bouncing from her hands, flew towards me.
I could barely keep my balance after such a pass and awkwardly tossed it over the net. Kira annoys me. I don't know why...
As she ran past me again, Kira got tripped. She stumbled, flew a few meters, and fell into the dirt. The sequence ended with the ball landing on her head.
The other classmates gathered around her, worried and whispering.
Kira looks sadly at her scraped, bleeding elbows and knees, her scratched palms. A bead of sweat hangs from her nose.
Sweat and dirt immediately stick to her legs and arms. She looks straight at me, understanding the reason for her fall.
-Why?
I looked away. A fight might start now.
-Mira, I... I'm not your enemy. I don't de-serve... th-is...
Kira wiped her wet nose with her hand and stood up.
-I know I can be ir-ritat-ing... I'm try-ing to be bet-ter.
-Guys, I'm fine... I just need to wash up...
Kira headed to the shower to clean up and change.
-Mira, you're getting F
-Yeah, got it.
I turned and left the sports field too, to calm down.
Damn, I don't know what's gotten into me. Where is all this hatred for Kira coming from? She only just joined our class...
I know for sure - something's wrong with her, but what? I can't explain it to myself... I can't put it into words. Maybe I should get to know her better - maybe this feeling will go away.
Sonya's already here, in the classroom. Skipped class. As usual...
-Hey! You look... different? Why the sad face? Why are you all sweaty? Were you at gym?
-Yeah, and I really shouldn't have... So...
The door opened, and there was Kira - smelling of fruity perfume and wearing makeup - as if nothing happened during the last class.
She was wearing strange old-fashioned gold jewelry, and overall, if she didn't look her sixteen years, you'd think she was someone's mom.
The students immediately surrounded her, introducing themselves and asking her questions about everything. Kira now seems like the alpha girl or something.
I wonder if this will last, or if everyone will get tired of her in a couple of days... She spotted Sonya and me and pushed her way over to our desk.
She extended her hand to Sonya a bit too enthusiastically, shaking it in a handshake.
It somehow really touched me. Fine, if it's that important to her, why not?
-Let's go! I'd love to.
-Great!
Alina looked genuinely happy.
-You've got something planned, right?
-Well... yeah? I guess you could say that.
Alina headed somewhere toward the riverbank, and I followed her.
-Are we going to the river?
-Yeah.
The mood was just wonderful. Instead of boring classes, I'm going to the river with Alina. Swimming might be too cold, but I'm not a fan anyway - for me, the best part is sunbathing on the shore.
Although the tan turns out rather pale, barely noticeable - it's still wonderful to sit on the sand and watch the water splash and the seagulls cry.
-I woke up today to a strange sound. Like a siren going off outside... I hid under the blanket and barely managed to fall back asleep...
-So you heard it too? I wasn't imagining it...
-Is it... something serious?
-I don't think so. Probably someone made a mistake.
-Got it... Still, it's very creepy!
The path we were walking turned into the forest. The city dust in my lungs was immediately replaced by air filled with the smell of damp earth, moss, and resin.
I finally took a deep breath.
-We're here!
Alina stopped by a huge, sprawling tree. It seemed bigger and older than any tree on this shore.
You could dance around the petrified trunk covered in cracked bark and moss during festivals - it's that huge.
The tree's crown spread somewhere high up in the sky, and to see it, I had to tilt my head back.
Pieces of rebar were hammered into the trunk, forming a kind of ladder that you could climb up.
-It's so big...
-Yes! Despite all the times this oak has been hurt and scarred with iron, it keeps growing... Mira, can you climb trees?
Indeed - the rusty rods were wrapped in wood, having long since become part of the tree itself.
-I don't know... Honestly, I haven't tried. What about you?
-Yes, watch... It's not hard at all!
Alina easily stepped on the spikes up to the first big branch, hugged it with her arms, and climbed up.
Her body looked so... Wild... There was an ancient, forgotten grace about it. Her movements were so light and airy. Alina crouched down, resting her hands on the tree trunk like a cat.
-Wow... And your hand... Doesn't it hurt?
Alina shook her head.
-I've learned to manage without it. So... Are you coming?
I hesitantly stepped onto the steel rod.
-Will it hold me?
-You're slim; it'll hold.
The iron rod slightly bent, bouncing me up and down, disturbing my shaky balance.
Alina's compliment boosted my confidence, and, clinging to bits of bark, I reached the second and third spikes, holding my breath.
After which, I grabbed the bark with my nails. I need help...
-Will you help me?
-Sure.
Alina clung to the tree trunk and extended her hand to me. Trying not to hurt her too much, I pulled myself up, and there we were on the lower branch.
Not bad, but this is just the beginning. I need to gather my strength if I want to make it to the top with Alina. I looked at my hands, which were already pretty scraped and burning.
-I'm tired...
-What? Already?
-You want to go all the way to the very top, right?
-Yeah.
Alina nodded affirmatively.
Oh, we have a long way to go...

Swearing under my breath and risking falling down time and again, I climbed branch by branch, following Alina up the oak tree. I tried not to look down, but it was impossible - I had to keep an eye on my feet.
Following Alina's example, I thought to take off my sneakers, then I tied the laces together and hung them around my neck.
It was easier to grip the rough bark with bare feet.
Alina glanced at me from time to time, smiled to herself, and climbed higher confidently.
Finally, we were almost at the top.
A branch with an unobstructed view.
The view sent shivers through me. A thrill ran through my body from a gust of wind.
I squinted and leaned closer to the gap in the leaves. Through half-closed eyes, I could see the endless misty expanse across both sides of the river.
I can't describe the feeling that seizes me here at the top. Such freshness, such... Freedom. Freedom and fear. It's... so beautiful.
-Sit down.
Alina patted the massive branch beside her, and we sat down together.
-Did you happen to bring any cookies?
I actually did have cookies with me. I handed the pack to Alina.
-You feel right at home here.
Alina paused for a moment and gave me a strange look.
-No. I just feel good here.
-Definitely better than at school.
-You're right. It's... hard to be around people. And when there are so many... I completely lose myself. My thoughts become like dots and dashes, and I can't even understand them myself.
-And then you have to study... Remember things... It's so hard.
-You don't like people?
-No, it's not that... I think it's more that... that they don't like me. I constantly feel like I've done something wrong.
-If someone's laughing, I'm sure they're laughing at me. If they're whispering about something... It's definitely about me!
I couldn't think of anything to say. People really can be cruel. Though that's not always the case.
Alina sat quietly, looking off into the distance, holding the cookie package in her hands. She slowly put one in her mouth and started thinking.
-What are you thinking about?
-M-m?
-Counting crows?
-I m-mph mph-mphmp.
I shrugged, and Alina took the cookie out of her mouth.
-See, over there, in the distance?
-What exactly?
-Well, the power lines.
-Yes, poles, wires. And?
-They cut a tunnel through the forest to put up those...
-Without the wires, there wouldn't be a Net.
-Yeah... And each time, there are more and more of these tunnels... The wires are wrapping around the city. The city is carving deep wounds in the forest, and soon, nothing will be left of it.
-Bodhi will die soon too.
-Bodhi? You mean this tree?
-Yes. That's why I try to visit it often.
-I didn't know you liked plants so much.
-Oh, I really do! My whole house is full of them.
We sat there, on the treetop, exposed to all the winds, but even so, I felt calm and cozy next to Alina.
Her kind, innocent face looked like a big, sweet, round pancake.
-Look what I have.
-Soap bubbles?
-Yep!
I had almost forgotten this was a thing. The last time I blew bubbles was when I was about eight. Alina dipped the ring into the little bottle, covering it with a shiny, oily film.

Alina took a deep breath and began slowly blowing a transparent bubble. It wobbled and twisted, and finally, when it got big, it detached from the ring and floated into the sky, twirling and spinning in the breeze.
-You're really good at that.
-Thank you! Now you try.
Alina handed me the bottle. Not that I'm sure of my skills... I blew a couple of small, awkward bubbles.
We laughed like kids at the big, clumsy bubbles floating around us. Some burst right in front of our faces, but that made it even more fun.
Eventually, the bottle ran out.
-Shall we go? My nose is getting cold.
I agreed.
My stiff body climbed back down the branches with difficulty. For some reason, going down was scarier than going up.
I placed my foot on the first metal rung. My foot slipped, and I lost my balance.
The fall wasn't long - a moment later, I was on the ground.
-Mira, are you okay?
-Yeah, just... My head's buzzing. Hopefully, it'll pass...
-Alright... Maybe it's best if you go home. I'll walk you.
-No big deal. I think we're still on time for class - don't you want to go to school?
-School? I thought... you don't really like studying.
-What do you mean?
-I didn't mean to offend you, sorry... Please forgive me...
-No need to apologize, you're right. But... Maybe there'll be something fun?
Alina shrugged.
-Let's go. We really are on time.
We returned to the school gates.
-I think I've come to terms with your tendencies. How about we plan the next date with a cat?
-You don't mind, right?
School isn't really about lessons and learning. It's about friends, acquaintances, some jokes, and carefree moments. If I want to learn something, I can do it all at home.
We peeked into the classroom. The teacher had stepped out, and part of the class had dispersed to interest clubs.
I noticed Sonya standing next to an unfamiliar girl.
She looked quite unusual - tall, strict clothing, shiny gold accessories. I decided to get closer.
-Oh, hey. We haven't introduced ourselves. -I'm Kira!
The girl extended her hand to me a bit too eagerly, shaking it in a handshake.
-I'm new here.
-I see... We also had a new student yesterday - his name was Kir.
-Kir is my bro-ther.
-Wow... He didn't mention you.
-So... You came here with him?
The girl has a heavy lisp, and it's jarring.
-Buh-buh-buh. No sur-prise, we don't get along at all.
-So... You came here with him?
I've read so much about th-is city...
-There's stuff written about us?
-Yeah... "A city under a night veil." If it were eas-ier to get here, many would come to see the endless night.
-Good thing it's not actually endless...
-Yeah...
-Kira, your outfit... So this is what they wear there, outside?
-"Out-side," you mean, from where I came?
I nodded affirmatively.
Kira glanced away, embarrassed.
-It's just... I don't know much about clo-thes... Do I look si-lly?
Sonya joined the conversation, fearing I might say something awkward again.
-No-no, not at all! You look cool. Very original!
-Thanks... You know, it's really hard to find ni-ce things in my si-ze. Even in shopping cen-ters.
-Shopping center? What's that?
Kira probably felt like some kind of explorer at that moment.
-Oh, well... it's like a big building with lots and lots of different stores, or something like that.
-Whoa... So, like our market!
-Sonya!
-What?
-You girls are s-o funny!
Kira is the complete opposite of her brother. She literally radiates warmth and kindness. It feels like if you put them together, they'd make a perfect magnet.
Maybe I should get to know Kira better?
-Or get to know what's in her wallet. These city kids don't understand the value of money!
-Maybe we'll get something out of it too?
-Hey, what about hanging out together after classes? Well, if you're not busy or anything...
-Uh... Sure, that sounds great! It'll be fun to get to know each other better! We could even play ball together.
-Deal.
-You'll pay me back eventually... Anyway, later.

It's only Tuesday, and I'm already sick of the school bell. 
I gestured for Kira to follow me; she quickly put her things away and was by my side with Sonya in an instant.
-Let's stock up on Raze.
I rummaged through my pockets, but they were empty.
Kira pulled a folded bill out of her small, funny-looking purse.
-Pay me back eventually... Anyway, later.
We dashed out of school and headed for the kiosk across the street.
-Ma'am, five of those nice cans.
-That's a hundred and five.
-*whispering* Shit, we only have a hundred...
-Could we bring the rest later?
The woman thought for a moment and agreed, and soon we were walking down the street, giddy, with a black bag.
-So, it's Kira's treat?
-Yep.

We opened the fizzy cans. This time we got lucky, and the drink hardly foamed up. "Caffeine + Taurine. Contains alcohol, approved for ages 18 and up." Yeah, yeah... Sure, I'll listen to you, little can.
I took a swig of the sour-sweet "Raze." A chemical fruity-alcoholic taste. Just wonderful!
Even though the city is barely lit - the sky is filled with a dim yellow light, and it feels like the streets are covered by a dirty glass dome that blocks out the starlight.
-And what good are all the trams rushing around? We're still stuck under this dome. And it's here to stay...
-Sonya, do you think... are we alone in the universe?
-What difference does it make? And anyway, who exactly is "we"?
-True... What difference does it make.
-Do you really feel so lonely on this planet that you need someone else?
-No, that's not really what I meant...
We arrived at a large concrete slab area - a good place to play.
Sonya tossed up the shared school ball and downed the last of her energy drink.
The ball was a bundle of rubber and fabric that made it look like some scruffy creature from our taiga.
I kicked the ball, and it arced toward Kira.
She skillfully caught it and passed it on.
-You play really well! Where'd you learn?
-I... don't know. It feels like I've always known how. And, well, my height helps too...
Kira blushed at her own words. I think she doesn't much like being so tall.
-Does it really bother you that much?
Kira took a small sip from her can and made a face.
-Honestly, if we're talking about boys... It's really a problem.
-No one's going to want to date me if I'm taller than them.
-Either way, the shorter the skirt, the more guys will flock around.
-That's rich, coming from someone whose skirt ends before you've even got a... well, you know.
Kira choked and dropped the ball.
-Honestly, Mira, that's not fair! You're in jeans, and we have to play in skirts!
-Sorry... Not my fault.
-All just to make us the center of attention.
-Hey!
The wet asphalt beneath our feet began to flash red and blue. Red, then blue again. I looked up. A police car. And a cop sitting on the hood.
Sonya and I immediately stopped.
-What's she doing here? And the lights are on... Did something happen?
-Sonya, hide the bag.
-Where am I supposed to hide it?
-In the bushes or something, just hurry up.
Sonya rustled her way over to some greenery, and I headed toward the police car. The cop spotted me almost immediately.
-Oh, Mira, hey!
It's Tolik. Him again.
-Not in school? Done already?
-Classes ended.
-Ah, I see. And how's Alya? Still studying?
I nodded.
-Got it... Well, look here...
Tolik pointed toward the wall of a nearby building.
-Probably can't see it... Hang on.
The bright beam of his police flashlight cut through the darkness, lighting up the wall...

Or rather, what was left of it - through a giant crack in the building, a mass of impossible, grotesque, pulsating flesh pushed through. I rubbed my eyes. Nothing changed, if anything, it only grew - veins, ulcers, webs of muscles filling my vision.

Why is this thing here? It looks like it belongs deep, deep underwater, or in some distant galaxy, where no one would ever see it. I'm losing it. Maybe this is just a dream? This just can't be real...
-Wh-what is that..?
-Don't know.
Tolik just shrugged.
-I came out for the call, and then saw this. Yep, it's looking at us. Wonder if it can hear us right now?
-W-why are you so calm?!
-Why not... I'm just sitting here thinking about what to do.
-What do you think is best - to get rid of this filth, or just cover it up somehow? Maybe no one will notice.
A rotten stench came from the wall of flesh, and the creature let out a deep, ancient groan.
-If at all possible... we need to get rid of this horror as soon as we can! It might kill someone, or destroy something else!
-I'll think about how we can do it. By the way...
Tolik pulled a gun from his holster and handed it to me.
-Wanna take a shot at it?
I held the cold gun in both hands. It was heavier than I thought... I raised the barrel, pointing it at the huge bubble-like eye staring right at me.
<<INTEGRATING...>
<<LOADING HUMAN INTERFACES...>>
<<ERROR: UNDEFINED BEHAVIOR>>
I pressed the trigger with all my strength, but it wouldn't budge. What the heck?
I silently handed the gun back.
-Couldn't do it? It's on the safety! No, we need a different approach. After all, it's night - we'll scare everyone this way. You know what, go home... You didn't bring anyone with you, did you?
-No, I'm alone.
-Good. And... Skipping school isn't good. If you skip again...
-What if this creature doesn't mean anyone harm?
-Even if it doesn't... Who knows what might happen if it suddenly gets angry.
-There's something to what you're saying...
-I'll think it over.
-You didn't bring anyone here, right?
-No, I'm alone.
-Good. And... Skipping school isn't good. If you skip again...
- Tolik shook his fist. -
-Alright, alright, I get it...
I couldn't tear my eyes away from the wall as I backed away. The flashlight's beam went out.
-Mira? What is that thing?
-We better go; I told him I was alone. Let's go quietly.
We ducked into the nearest courtyard and slipped away among the trees.
-I still can't shake it... I think I'm losing my mind...
Sonya was silent. She was probably shocked too.
-What did he say to you?

-Nothing. He didn't say anything... I...
I felt something... Near that creature... As if... As if it was calling me... All this time. And it's still calling... But why? What does it want?
-How is it calling you? What's it like?
-It's like my brain's picking up a radio signal, and the broadcast is playing directly in my mind!
-Sonya, I'm really, really scared!

-There's just too much going on...
 It all started yesterday when I saw the corpse in the bathroom, and then you gave me that computer...
-What? I gave it to you?
Sonya looked at me like I'd said something completely insane.
-Haha, no way, where would I get the money for that? I thought your mom bought it for you.
-Hmm...
Someday I'll deal with socializing.
-Ugh, gross, that's disgusting!
-It's just revolting!
-Huh?
-What happened?
I didn't immediately understand what was going on - classmates had gathered around one of the desks, all muttering in outrage.

I squeezed through the wall of bodies - in the center sat a bewildered Alya. Her gaze darted from face to face of those surrounding her, and at some point, her eyes landed on me. Her wet eyes were pleading for help.
-What's going on?
A girl from the crowd pointed to a pool of pus spreading across the desk, dripping down the table leg, and pooling on the linoleum.

I covered my mouth with my hand. Damn, that smell... Sweet, cloying, and sharp, like meat from a city market with a bitter undertone - such a crazy mix filled the entire classroom. I was sure I'd throw up. My head spun, and the frozen, terrified Alya blurred in my eyes.
-Alya... Let's go...
I pulled her from the crowd, and we ran to the girls' bathroom. The crowd followed us but stopped at the door.
-Alina, what happened?
It was impossible to stand near her - the strong smell immediately triggered a gag reflex.
-I... I... It's like... My hand... just burst...
Alina held out her bandaged hand. The bandages were soaked through with brown pus.
-Holy fuck... That's really bad... Maybe you should go to the hospital?
-No! No way!
-I knew it... Let me take a look...

I untied the knot on her wrist and unwrapped the first layer of bandage. Underneath was an even wetter layer, soaked with a foul-smelling slime.
I looked Alina sternly in the eyes.
-Why didn't you say anything?
Pointless...

I completely unwrapped the bandage. The last layer was especially hard to remove - part of it was stuck, glued by dried blood and pus to the skin. Beneath the gauze was decaying flesh covered with yellow blisters.

I looked at her unwrapped hand - Alina's hand was missing two fingers. Instead, there were ugly fresh scars. Her hand had been tightly bandaged, and the marks from the fabric's texture and folds ran across her skin. Her battered hand trembled and shook from the pain.
-You urgently need to clean the wounds and change the bandages. If you don't, they might have to amputate your hand.
-A-amputate? What should I do? I don't have bandages... Or anything...
I tore off a wad of toilet paper and dabbed at the wound.
-We need to see the nurse. Right now.
-But... She's not here this week...
Right... Fuck, fuck, fuck! What should we do? How do we get the supplies?
-I'm completely broke... But maybe... maybe we could sneak into the nurse's office ourselves?
-You mean... you want to...
-Yes, I want to steal medicine and bandages.
-That's a crime... Won't we get in trouble for it?
-If we're quiet, no one will know.
-Mira, I'm scared...
-And you're not scared of walking around with a festering wound?!
Alina shrank back, like a small, pissed kitten.
-That's better. Now let's go.
We waited until everyone in the hallway went back to class, then snuck over to the duty desk to take the necessary key off the hook, then made our way to the nurse's office.
-I think we can go inside, no one will find us here.
-Yeah... probably.
Alina quietly closed the door.
-Alright, here.
I handed Alina a handful of pills in different colors.
-Are you... sure these are the right pills?
-Well... uh... sort of.
-Alright. I trust you.
Alina swallowed the entire handful at once.
-Now comes the hard part...
-It's going to hurt a lot.
-N-no! Don't make it hurt! Please, no!
-This is alcohol; it will disinfect the wounds. But it's going to sting...
-A-are you sure you're doing this right?
-Yes... I'm sure.
Alina calmed down a little, then I rolled up a towel and told her to bite down on it.
-Sit down and give me your hand.
I took Alina's battered hand and, gripping it tightly, poured the bottle of green antiseptic over her festering wounds.
-Ready?
Alina's eyes rolled back, and she barely breathed.
-I'm pouring the second bottle...
The green liquid mixed with blood spilled onto the floor, dripping down her trembling hand.
-There. Let's bandage it, and you'll live.
-Damn, I can't find anything. Just bandages. Nothing else.
-How's that...
-So... is this the end for me? Am I going to die?
-No... We'll think of something...
Everything was turned upside down. Sheets with student files, parasite tests, blood tests, stool and urine analyses, strange pills - all mixed into one mess, soaked in a hospital atmosphere.

We decided to leave the mess as it was.
I looked into the guard's room and left the nurse's office key there. That's it.
-Maybe you really should go to the hospital?
-No! No way! Even if I die, I'm not going there!
I could barely hold back my anger. My teeth ground so loudly Alina could hear it.
-Alright. Let's go see the TRUD teacher.
-Uh... okay, but why?

The workshop classroom was on the first floor, just like the nurse's office. We cracked the door open - it was unlocked, which meant the teacher was somewhere inside. The classroom was empty - so he must be in the backroom.
-Shh, let's go...
We crept along, half-crouched, to the backroom.
As I expected, the shop teacher was sitting there, holding a huge bottle of alcohol, with a loaf of black bread drying nearby.
-There. Alcohol. We'll disinfect your wounds with this.
-Hey, Palych!
-Who's there? Ah, you little prostitutes... What do you want?
-We need to use some alcohol.
The teacher's bloodshot, fish-like eyes stared at us with suspicion.
-Isn't it a bit early for you to start buhat'? Still little hookers, aren't you.
-Alina, show him your hand.
-Huh? Show it?
Alina unwrapped her damp bandage and extended her hand to the teacher.
The old man squinted at her injuries and broke off a piece of bread.
-Come here, come closer.
Alina timidly stepped closer.
The wound under the bandages looked terrible. The festering blisters had burst in some places, oozing dirty yellow pus.
The old man took a swig of alcohol, grabbed Alina's wrist, and scooped up the pus with a piece of bread. He then popped the pus-soaked bread into his mouth.
-Ahh, damn! That hit the spot...
I shuddered and let out a weak scream.
What the fuck?
Alina's face showed the maximum possible disgust, fear, and panic.
The old man pressed a cloth to the wound, which squirted pus in all directions, and then generously poured alcohol over it from the bottle.
-Ah, this alcohol... Such a waste... Well, take care, stay healthy!
We ran out of the classroom immediately.
While Alina was recovering from the shock, I awkwardly wrapped her hand.
-Th... thank you... Mira...
-You really should go to the hospital... Who knows what this might turn into...
-No... I can't... go to the hospital...
I took in the mess. Red-green puddles on the floor and dirty bandages. We'd better get out of here quickly.
-Shall we go?
Alina obediently trudged along behind me.
-I need... to go to the bathroom...
It seems I mixed up the pills...
It doesn't make sense to go back to class. I'm going home...
The way home felt long and hard. I started thinking about how hungry I was.
No wonder - I haven't eaten in a couple of days.
-Leaving again without saying goodbye.
-Mind if I walk with you? Listen, I was starving this morning... Anyway, I miscalculated my strength, and... well, do you want some?
Sonya handed me a half-eaten, steamed bun wrapped in paper.
-You have no idea how perfect your timing is.

Without a second thought, I grabbed it and took a bite of the round, fluffy bun.
 The taste of cabbage and fried meat with spicy pepper...

It's the best thing I've ever eaten in my life! 
 Sonya struggled to hold back her laughter as I stuffed my cheeks like a hamster, but eventually, she couldn't help herself.
-What's so funny?
-N-nothing...

While we walked along the path, Sonya told me something about fashion magazines and her favorite TV show, but I barely remembered any of it. My head was filled with the events of the day, and they refused to leave.
Finally, I finished the bun. Now I could stop thinking about festering wounds, blood, and monsters.
-So, what do you think?
-Huh?
-About Laura Palmer.
-Oh, yeah. She's so cool!
Sonya laughed.
-I knew you weren't listening.
-I wanted to ask you... about the "Spam."
Right before my eyes, all the cheerfulness drained from Sonya's face, as if it had been washed away by rain.
-Why are you quiet?
-Why do you care?
-So, you got hold of stims...
-Why does it matter to you! Here you go again...
-Can't you understand! I'm worried about you!
-If you valued me, you would've never messed with this junk!
My attempts to talk her out of it once again ended in failure. It was useless.
-Why are you so... weird? Cats can't talk... And... why can only I see you?
-I'm not weird. I'm special.
The cat purred, slowly stretching his purple-clawed paws.
-You probably already guessed. We're all fragments of a giant puzzle, pieces of information, immersed in an endless cosmic abyss, you know.
-You look like monsters from nightmares.
-Monsters, am I?
The cat gave me a sly wink with one eye, and a chill ran down my spine from his gaze.
-I am a reflection. Of your fantasies or your fears.
-I materialized from your desires, your programs. From the things you love...
-From... Pokemon?
I blurted out the word without thinking.
-Maybe...
The cat purred with a sly smile.
I've been thinking. Since this kitty wants to live with me...
-I'll name you Purr-purr.
The name came to mind on its own. It was as if it had always belonged to him, and I just remembered it suddenly.
